processing_notes: Source confirms zero cholera transmission 1975-01-01..1975-11-30. Source states: 'Le Niger est demeuré indemne de choléra depuis 1974 en dépit de la réintroduction de cas bactériologiques à la suite du pèlerinage de 1975 à La Mecque.'. Evidence type: Documented_Absence. Surveillance system status during absence: operational. Explicit WHO country-office statement that Niger remained free of cholera from 1974 to the time of writing (between Apr and Oct 1976). The only exception it names is the reintroduction of bacteriologically confirmed cases after the 1975 Hajj (Dhu al-Hijjah 1395 = December 1975), so this zero row stops at 30 Nov 1975 and the pilgrim importations are recorded as a presence record (Dec 1975-Jan 1976). Corroboration: WER 'Cholera in 1975' (WER 51(18)) Table 1 lists no Niger notification, and Niger is absent from the 1975 WER notifications index. Surveillance: weekly notifiable-disease bulletin functioning (the profile notes collation errors) and laboratory detection of imported cases shows case detection was operating. National level. [AGENT 3 REVISION 2026-10-03] EXTENDED by Agent 3 (2026-10-03): TL 1975-01-01 -> 1974-08-18, so that one row spans the continuous absence. The WHO country office states Niger 'est demeure indemne de cholera depuis 1974' (this source); the 1974 WER cholera index lists Niger only on pp.94, 103, 195, 226, 260, 315, the last (WER 49(37), metadata 147) carrying the notifications of 28.VII-3.VIII and 11-17.VIII.1974 (1 case each), and the notified 1974 series sums to the WHO annual (287 vs 286/75; Agent 1) - so no case after 17 Aug 1974. The Hajj importations of Dec 1975-Jan 1976 remain a presence record. (reason: Agent 3: zero period extended to the end of the 1974 outbreak (continuous absence, one row)) [AGENT 4 REVISION 2026-10-03] Agent 4 corroboration (primary, US Embassy Niamey cable 1975NIAMEY00594, 13 Feb 1975, https://search.wikileaks.org/plusd/cables/1975NIAMEY00594_b.html): Vice President Sani Sido told a US Senate staff delegation on 11 Feb 1975 that the western mobile health team 'had recently been assigned task of inoculating all El Hadj pilgrims returning from Mecca where they had been exposed to cholera and had succeeded in avoiding outbreak of cholera'. The Dec 1974 Hajj had the largest pilgrimage cholera outbreak in recent years, starting among Nigerian pilgrims and exported by returning hajjis (US Embassy Jidda cables 1975JIDDA00006, 1 Jan 1975, and 1975JIDDA00282, 14 Jan 1975). This supports no outbreak in Jan-Feb 1975. DATING CAVEAT: the WHO country profile's 'reintroduction de cas bacteriologiques a la suite du pelerinage de 1975' may refer to these Jan-1975 returns rather than the Dec-1975 Hajj (Saudi Arabia also notified 50 cases in 1976, WER 52(19)), so bacteriologically positive importations (count unknown) may fall inside this row's Jan 1975 window; no count found, row kept. (reason: Agent 4: primary 1975 cable corroboration and dating caveat) [AGENT 4 REVISION 2026-10-03] Agent 4 corroboration (WHO monthly returns): World Health Statistics Report 29(3) (1976) p.118, Table 1.1 Cholera (https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/75255): Niger 1975 entries '-' (nil) for Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May and Jul 1975 (Jun, Aug-Dec '+' = not yet received); WHSR 29(9) (1976) p.480 Table 1.1 (https://iris.who.int/handle/10665/75253), which lists the African countries reporting cholera in 1975 or 1976 (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Cape Verde, Comoros, Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Mozambique, Nigeria, Southern Rhodesia, Uganda, Cameroon, Upper Volta), omits Niger.
